chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakhai narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Salim from his father from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him). He said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) had two rings. The inscription on one of them was: 'There is no god but Allah, a preparation for the meeting with Allah.' And the inscription on the other was: 'Indeed, Allah brings about His command.'
And the inscription on the ring of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was: 'Disgraced and wretched is the murderer of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both).'

key_terms.خاتم: Signet ring, used for sealing and as a personal symbol
key_terms.عدة للقاء الله: Preparation for the meeting with God, expressing readiness for death
key_terms.نقش: Inscription or engraving on a ring

ai.seo_question: What were the ring inscriptions of Imam Husayn and Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS), transmitted via Imam al-Sadiq (AS), describes the ring inscriptions of Imam Husayn (AS) and Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS). Husayn's two rings bore messages of monotheism and trust in divine providence, while his son Sajjad's ring expressed condemnation of his father's murderers. This narration, delivered at al-Saduq's assembly on the first of Muharram 367 AH, reflects how the Imams carried their deepest convictions on their personal effects.
